pages.text: Dingding planted beans at the bank's end. Days passed. Only dark earth showed.
Dingding touched the soil. Sunny side warm, shaded side still cold. "When will my beans come up?"
Grandma counted on fingers. "Ten days should have done it."
She gently dug. The bean was still there.
"Lazy beans this year." She dug elsewhere too.
Earth scattered from each dug place. Not one sprout.
Dingding worried. "Keep digging, and they may never come up."
Dingding peered at the warm soil. One tiny green dot!
"Here, Grandma!" Beside it, another and another.
Grandma covered her digging and patted the soil. "Never wake children who are sleeping in."
